shoal_e02_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_entry.text: On Day Two Hundred Twenty-Three, the quarantine gate opened onto a wet strip of stone. Yue had arrived early enough to watch a clerk replace yesterday's chalk marks. Her observation interval was complete, but her name had not yet been called. A woman in front of her held a covered basket away from the rain. Behind her, a boy asked his father whether the port would keep his shoes if they smelled of another town.

shoal_e02_wait_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_01.text: Sui's receiving station had three entrances with different purposes. Travelers entered through the narrow pedestrian gate; cargo stopped before a painted rail; current workers used a checked side passage after their own morning inspection. Yue did not cross the worker passage because her proposed job had a line on a clerk's desk. The distinction mattered to the men waiting there. A visitor entering as staff would make their delay look like a personal failure.

shoal_e02_wait_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_02.text: She offered the room keepers' dated receipts and her own travel record. Sui read the dates before looking at the cultivation certificate. No certificate could shorten a disease observation interval by making its bearer useful. Yue had felt no fever, unusual cough, or new skin change. She answered for herself. When the clerk asked whether anyone on the carrier had been ill, she described what she had actually seen and admitted the limits of a passenger's knowledge.

shoal_e02_wait_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_03.text: The covered basket held bread for a baker's sister working inside. The woman had traveled from a nearby licensed district and needed a different inspection from Yue's. A clerk opened the basket with permission and found a note beneath the cloth. He did not read it aloud. The note's private language could not establish whether the bread met cargo rules. The woman looked so relieved by this small separation that Yue felt embarrassed to have been expecting an argument.

shoal_e02_wait_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_04.text: A dock hand coughed into his elbow while waiting at the worker passage. Two people stepped away; a third laughed too quickly and said everyone coughed beside salt water. Sui sent the hand to the ordinary clinical desk and temporarily removed his access token from the active queue. His employer's wage clerk would have to answer the work question. The quarantine captain neither diagnosed him nor pretended that a missed shift was merely a matter of attitude.

shoal_e02_wait_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_05.text: The clinical desk charged against a separately funded inspection account, not Yue's proposed care reserve. Its practitioner asked the man about duration, sleep, and the rooms where he had spent the night. He could name the people he had close contact with privately. Yue stayed outside hearing range. A public gate needed public rules; an ordinary person being examined still deserved a space that did not turn his body into entertainment for everyone waiting.

shoal_e02_wait_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_06.text: Rain gathered at the inspection table's downhill leg. Yue could have nudged the water along with a cloth, but the clerk was already calling a paid attendant whose morning task included keeping that surface dry. She stepped aside. Her tendency to help first and ask later had once seemed harmless. Here it could hide the fact that the attendant had been assigned too many tables, while making a visitor appear more reliable than a worker who was already busy.

shoal_e02_wait_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_07.text: Sui called Yue through to the marked square. The harbor needed to know her current application limit only because an accepted technical task might put her near equipment later. Yue gave the tested figures without embellishment: half a unit over four ordinary breaths, a quarter useful, independently stopped and grounded, recovered throughput no greater than an eighth per breath. Six primary pairs described what she had earned; they did not authorize a harbor-sized discharge.

shoal_e02_wait_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_08.text: The captain examined the certificate's date and witness marks. She did not ask Yue to demonstrate at the quarantine gate. A demonstration there would provide neither a suitable stop nor a calibrated load and would put bystanders inside an unnecessary trial. She noted the waist-work clearance and the old shoulder limitation. A foreman who wanted overhead help would have to hire someone qualified for it. Yue could refuse without explaining her entire injury to that foreman.

shoal_e02_wait_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_09.text: A man behind the cargo rail recognized her name and asked whether she could sterilize his tar barrels. Yue said she had no tested application that could do so. Sui added that an untested energy treatment would invalidate their inspection rather than replace it. The man looked disappointed, then asked the cargo clerk for the ordinary treatment price. His disappointment was reasonable. Yue could accept it without offering a larger claim to make the moment pleasant.

shoal_e02_wait_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_10.text: Her own pack contained clothing, personal notes, a small unpowered practice strip, and the objects listed under the separately declared incoming contract. The inspector followed that declaration instead of guessing ownership from the cultivation paper. Items requiring different custody stayed under their existing receipt conditions. No blanket stamp made a private source public or turned borrowed material into Yue's property. She asked for that distinction to appear before signing the general pack entry.

shoal_e02_wait_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_11.text: The inspector found a cedar splinter lodged in a coat seam. Yue had acquired it on the road while helping hold a crate lid at ordinary waist height. It had no special meaning. He removed it with permission and put it in the waste bowl rather than presenting it like a recovered omen. She laughed at her own relief. A story about an unfamiliar traveler could acquire a symbol with alarming ease when bored people watched every object leave her pack.

shoal_e02_wait_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_12.text: Han brought the room-extension options to the waiting bench. The original eight nights were finished. Yue could pay three more nights from her own settled savings at the same posted two-copper daily rate, while she inspected the proposed employment conditions. She agreed to six copper for Days Two Hundred Twenty-Three through Two Hundred Twenty-Five. No port grant extended automatically. Whatever she chose about the job, she would not leave a keeper holding an unspoken housing promise.

shoal_e02_wait_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_13.text: Port entry finally produced a narrow permission: ordinary access to the licensed lanes and specified public buildings, not free movement through stores, moored vessels, or active rigging yards. Yue received a current map with shaded boundaries. The clerk warned her that a dry lane could still close while a mast was lowered. A permit did not make moving work stop for its holder. She read the route to the public introduction before putting the map away.

shoal_e02_wait_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_14.text: The bread woman passed inside after her own inspection. The coughing dock hand remained at the clinical desk while an assistant fetched his wage representative. Neither outcome described everyone at the gate. Yue wanted a neat conclusion to the morning because the wet waiting had exhausted her. Instead, she left with her own permission and the knowledge that the next person still had a different problem. The harbor would not become simpler merely because she had been admitted.

shoal_e02_wait_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_15.text: Beyond the gate, the public lane curved around the burned lamp store. Its empty doorway had been braced, and a warning rope kept pedestrians away from loose masonry. Yue stopped outside the rope. She could see scorched grooves under a surviving shelf, but these were old damage with no dated witness attached. They might guide a future qualified inspection. They could not explain a different fire that had not happened, or establish whose negligence had caused the old one.

shoal_e02_wait_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_16.text: An ordinary laborer pushed a cart of approved replacement stone past her. He was rebuilding a drain, not reconstructing the lamp store. Two funded projects could occupy the same lane without belonging to one recovery account. He asked her to move her boot from the chalk crossing mark. She did. The stone scraped over the cart's worn wheel in a rhythm too regular to sound dramatic. A city repaired itself through such work long before any visitor understood its budget.

shoal_e02_wait_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_17.text: At the packing partnership room, He Ming was arguing with a merchant about an empty crate. The merchant wanted its return before a delayed boat arrived; He Ming said the crate belonged to the household packing cooperative under a separate lease. Neither asked Yue to decide. She waited until they reached their own provisional arrangement, then accepted the public introduction leaflet. An outsider's education in other people's terms did not confer authority to settle them.

shoal_e02_wait_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_18.text: The leaflet placed current hands, displaced hands, suppliers, and residents at different speaking tables so that the loudest group could not consume the whole afternoon. Anyone could attend the public introduction without accepting a job. Formal testimony would need separate permission later. Yue disliked the idea of a dispute chopped into timed pieces, but He Ming pointed to the people who would otherwise wait until midnight. Fairness sometimes sounded like a clerk asking a speaker to stop.

shoal_e02_wait_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_19.text: She offered to carry a stack of chairs. The keeper assigned her four at a time and told her not to lift above her cleared waist range. The work was ordinary and unpowered. A younger porter carried a larger stack past her without making a point of it. Yue felt the familiar temptation to explain that she could circulate through six pairs now. She left the explanation unsaid. The port did not owe her an audience for a smaller safe load.

shoal_e02_wait_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_20.text: Before the introduction began, a resident asked whether cultivation could detect a hidden fever. Yue said her present training did not qualify her to diagnose other people's bodies. The ordinary practitioner had a separate examination method, and the resident could choose to attend that desk. The question had been hopeful rather than foolish. Yue answered it gently without claiming an ability she might one day learn. Possibility was a poor substitute for available care when someone needed help today.

shoal_e02_wait_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_21.text: The supervisor candidate arrived carrying the restoration proposal rolled around a wooden gauge. His qualification came from ordinary comparison work and a current fire-safety signoff. He had never taught Yue's bodily practice. He asked her to describe how an independent stop would work when he controlled the equipment boundary. She explained her release stroke, then asked what he would do if she failed to respond. He showed the unpowered external stop before discussing any future test.

shoal_e02_wait_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_22.text: His answer was less flattering than she had expected. If she became unable to stop, he would end the trial, preserve the load record, and send her for qualified care. He would not keep calling her name while hoping that talent would fix the fault. He would also record his own part if he had allowed an inappropriate setup. Yue liked him more after that. A person whose plan included her failure might be safer than one who admired her success.

shoal_e02_wait_23.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_23.text: Rong listened from the supplier table and asked whether every useful quarter-unit needed such a large ring of precautions. The supervisor said a first local setup needed documented boundaries, after which routine permitted work could be quicker. It was an answer to the actual cost question, not a denunciation of commerce. Rong asked for the expected setup time. Suppliers could care about lost hours without thereby proving they were careless about lives. The answer still could not erase the stop.

shoal_e02_wait_24.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_24.text: Han kept the proposed thirty shifts on a separate page. Attendance at this introduction counted against neither accepted workdays nor the five-copper wage. Yue had not signed that acceptance. A resident who thought she was already paid for speaking challenged the distinction. Han opened the receiving allocation and showed what work its eight copper covered. Public figures could be misunderstood even when nobody had hidden them. The correction consumed part of an afternoon everyone had already planned to spend elsewhere.

shoal_e02_wait_25.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_25.text: A sail-tie repairer asked how many damaged parts would be examined and who would decide that a part could return to use. The supervisor's draft covered forty unloaded housings as a bounded comparison batch. Qualified signoff for any fueled application would remain separate. A housing Yue had touched could still be rejected. The repairer looked pleased by the refusal to promise restoration of everything. His own trade began with deciding what could not be mended safely.

shoal_e02_wait_26.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_26.text: Outside, the queue for the ordinary clinical desk had grown shorter. The coughing dock hand came through the public lane holding a temporary work restriction and a dated follow-up appointment. Yue did not ask for his diagnosis. He told He Ming that his wage representative had agreed to two paid restricted shifts sorting unpowered stock, under that employer's separate arrangement. It was a real accommodation, narrow enough to end or be changed after the follow-up rather than a general guarantee.

shoal_e02_wait_27.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_27.text: The introduction broke for water. A clerk offered Yue a chair at the officials' table, and she chose the edge nearest the public aisle so people could leave without crossing behind her. This was no declaration that every table had equal access. Some records remained private. It simply stopped her placement from turning a casual question into a summons. He Ming said the side door needed more room too, then went to move the chair that actually blocked it.

shoal_e02_wait_28.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_28.text: By the time discussion resumed, Yue had learned enough to ask a better question about the forty housings. Were rejected parts kept for evidence, returned to owners, or scrapped? The draft had merged all three into one arrow labeled disposal. Rong wanted the owners paid quickly. The supervisor wanted faults available for a second look. A packer wanted dangerous scrap kept away from the lane children. The arrow concealed a conflict that a larger wage would not settle.

shoal_e02_wait_29.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_29.text: Han proposed three separately marked containers and a scheduled owner decision after the safety review. No container would be emptied merely because a clerk needed its shelf. The materials allocation could buy the marks and closures, but it could not buy each owner's agreement to surrender property. Yue wrote the proposed change beneath her unsigned work terms. She could decide whether to take the role after seeing its boundaries. The afternoon had made those boundaries more demanding and more credible.

shoal_e02_wait_30.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_wait_30.text: As the tables began to clear, Yue's lodging arrangement determined which invitation she could accept before dark. People offered their own evening hours, not appointments she could claim on a room receipt. She could ask about another group's experience later through its public contact. Tonight, the eight-night beginning had already become a paid extension and a real pattern of who expected to find her near supper. She folded the public leaflet before following that expectation.

shoal_e02_lodging_gate.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_lodging_gate.text: The public introduction ended without a signed employment acceptance. Yue put the current lane map beside her own lodging receipt and left the partnership room. The keeper would expect her before the agreed closing hour. Whatever she had heard today would need checking against people whose routines continued after a public table had been cleared.

shoal_e02_guest_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_guest_01.text: At the receiving house, supper waited for the people whose shifts ended late rather than for the visitor with the most questions. Yue helped lay bowls without opening her notebook. The sail-tie repairer from the introduction arrived after the rice had been covered. His employer had not released him for the opening discussion. He wanted to know whether a vote had been taken before he reached the room. Yue said there had been proposals, not a vote.

shoal_e02_guest_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_guest_02.text: He listened to the three disposal containers and immediately asked who would guard them on a night shift. The supervisor's daytime safety plan had not answered that. Yue could add the question to the public draft if he permitted it; he chose an anonymous question because he still needed orders from a supplier likely to dislike a new delay. He did not authorize her to describe him as frightened, coerced, or a supporter of her future employment.

shoal_e02_guest_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_guest_03.text: His older cousin thought anonymity would make the question easier to ignore. He answered that being named would make his own next week's work harder. They argued while eating, and neither asked Yue to settle which courage was better. She copied the question without the private dispute. The household lodging had given her access to both statements. It had not given her the right to export a family disagreement as evidence of what all workers wanted.

shoal_e02_guest_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_guest_04.text: He Ming offered an introduction to a night sorter who might answer the actual guarding problem. The sorter could meet them outside the public partnership room after his paid work ended on Day Two Hundred Twenty-Five. It was a new appointment requiring the sorter's consent, not a benefit attached to the guest bed. Yue accepted the time. She would miss the courier inn's booking conversation that evening unless she requested a different commercial appointment.

shoal_e02_guest_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_guest_05.text: Rong's clerk replied that the current booking conversation would not be repeated privately this week. Yue could send specific public questions to the quay. She put the reply beside the night sorter's appointment rather than treating it as an insult. Her chosen access had a cost in current source detail. She could hear how rejected cargo affected wages before she could see precisely how a booking changed. Either account alone would leave part of the problem obscure.

shoal_e02_guest_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_guest_06.text: The keeper asked for the three-night extension money after the meal, using the same plain receipt as before. Yue paid six of her own copper for Days Two Hundred Twenty-Three through Twenty-Five. Household familiarity did not waive the rate. He Ming was nearby, but the keeper dealt with Yue directly so he would not appear to guarantee her debt. The room stayed a paid guest arrangement rather than a favor that a resident might later be asked to repay.

shoal_e02_guest_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_guest_07.text: That night, someone knocked on the screen to ask if Yue could examine a child's scraped finger. She declined the clinical role and fetched the house's ordinary clean-water bowl while the parent decided whether the practitioner was needed. She did not send qi into the wound. The parent took care of the scrape and thanked her for the bowl. A person could be helpful in a shared house without becoming its healer merely because she carried a cultivation certificate.

shoal_e02_guest_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_guest_08.text: Before sleeping, Yue marked the night sorter's guarding question as permission granted for an anonymous public addition. She left the cousin's criticism and the child's finger out. From the kitchen came the sound of a keeper counting tomorrow's meals. Her choice of bed had opened a practical question that the timed introduction missed. It had also made the limits of listening harder to ignore, because the people supplying that question would greet her again at breakfast.

shoal_e02_inn_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_inn_01.text: At the upstairs inn, Rong's booking conversation occupied the table beside the net seller's repaired weights. The merchant arrived with an ordinary clerk rather than a private technical appendix. Yue could ask about the sequence of a booking, but quoted prices and named customers remained outside this offered discussion. He paid for his own tea. The keeper collected Yue's separate three-night lodging extension at the posted rate before she sat down to listen.

shoal_e02_inn_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_inn_02.text: Six of Yue's own copper covered Days Two Hundred Twenty-Three through Twenty-Five. The inn keeper gave her a dated receipt and asked whether the extension was likely to continue after that. Yue said she would inspect the employment offer first. The keeper needed another answer by the twenty-fifth evening. A quiet room could still put a deadline on uncertainty. It did not become a free waiting space because a merchant had offered its guest a useful conversation.

shoal_e02_inn_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_inn_03.text: Rong described three canceled bookings without disclosing customer names. One failed because a cargo inspection was late; one because the shared carrier could not cross at the promised tide; one because a lender withdrew a reference tool before it was loaded. The booking forms had different cancellation marks. Yue was permitted to copy those public definitions, not the underlying private messages. What looked like a single late arrival at a kitchen could begin with very different obligations.

shoal_e02_inn_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_inn_04.text: The clerk pointed to a mark that Yue had read as a completed dispatch. It meant the request had been entered, not that anyone had carried it. Rong seemed amused that a careful traveler could make the same error as a hurried supplier. Yue corrected her own note. She did not ask the clerk to certify every booking she might later see. This conversation gave her a better reading method and a finite set of examples, not privileged access to the port's accounts.

shoal_e02_inn_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_inn_05.text: At the receiving house, the evening discussion about rejected parts continued without her. He Ming's message offered a public appointment with a night sorter after his shift on Day Two Hundred Twenty-Five, but Yue already had a scheduled follow-up with the booking clerk then. She asked for the anonymous guarding question in writing if its owner consented. The answer might arrive later. Choosing the inn's commercial access had cost the unplanned time in which household questions could be followed immediately.

shoal_e02_inn_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_inn_06.text: Rong asked whether she would accept the salvage job now that she knew how dispatch errors occurred. Yue said its physical limits, owner returns, and night guarding still needed inspection. He did not offer to pay her wage privately to hurry the decision. He wanted a reliable batch more than an eager signature. His interest could align with her caution for a while without making him a benefactor whose future claims she must accept.

shoal_e02_inn_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_inn_07.text: When the net seller needed the table for a late repair, the meeting ended. Yue helped move the cups and kept her notes away from the cutting surface. A courier invited her upstairs to hear a more exciting account of a smuggled lamp. She declined because the speaker would not identify which details he had observed. A private room had given her a place to stop working. She used it rather than turning every evening story into a new investigation.

shoal_e02_inn_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_inn_08.text: In her room, Yue separated permitted booking definitions from the clerk's unquoted examples. She could use the definitions to ask public questions tomorrow. She could not circulate private customers' inferred problems. The receiving house might supply an experience she lacked, if its residents chose to meet later. The inn had shown her a paper distinction with real consequences: requesting a journey was not making one. That would matter more when someone began counting on a dispatch.

shoal_e02_rejoin_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_01.text: On the morning of Day Two Hundred Twenty-Four, Yue followed the newly permitted lane to the current public notice board. A strip of fresh paint stopped visitors at a repair site that yesterday's borrowed map had shown as open. She turned back to the posted alternate route. Her permit covered licensed lanes as they actually existed, not a personal right to demand the shorter path. The detour brought her past a yard where damaged sailcloth dried on frames.

shoal_e02_rejoin_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_02.text: A worker tried to push an empty handcart through the repair barrier, saying he had used that path all winter. The attendant pointed to the open trench and the alternate route's width. The worker could wait for the scheduled crossing escort or go around. He chose to wait and grumbled about the lost quarter-hour. Yue shared his impatience without volunteering to carry the cart over the trench. Her bodily clearance and the trench's current condition did not support that shortcut.

shoal_e02_rejoin_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_03.text: When the escort opened the marked crossing, the cart's wheel caught a loose edge. Two attendants used an ordinary plank under the wheel while the worker eased the handle back. Yue remained outside the crossing lane. Nothing dramatic happened, and that was the value of the prepared route. Later, someone might tell the story as a near disaster avoided by a cultivator who happened to stand nearby. She had contributed nothing to the maneuver and would say so.

shoal_e02_rejoin_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_04.text: At the public office, Sui's assistant asked if any new symptoms had appeared after entry. Yue answered the routine question and returned her borrowed current map for the week's update. The assistant showed her how temporary lane closures were stamped with an expiry and a review time. A closure that expired still needed a current inspection before reopening. Yue copied that instruction. A faded barrier could be dangerous precisely because everybody remembered it as an old inconvenience.

shoal_e02_rejoin_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_05.text: The ordinary practitioner came out to collect clean cloth delivered from a different district. He carried a list of approved quantities but did not say which patients would use them. Yue asked whether the proposed restoration care reserve could be treated as clinical access for its workers. He said a reserve could pay actual permitted care charges; it could not diagnose illness or guarantee recovery. That sentence belonged in the employment terms before anyone imagined forty copper made bodily risk disappear.

shoal_e02_rejoin_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_06.text: She visited the forty proposed housings under the supervisor's observation. Today she only looked. The parts lay in owner-labeled rows, some sound outside and some visibly warped. Their fuel sockets had been blocked before the visit. The supervisor refused to uncover a latch just to satisfy a visitor's curiosity without a safe work setup. Yue could accept his refusal because a later accepted shift might provide the right time. She did not need the inspection to become a demonstration.

shoal_e02_rejoin_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_07.text: One housing had a narrow strip of red cloth tied beneath its handle. The owner had used it to distinguish a repaired family shipment from an untouched one. It was not a hazard rating. A clerk had copied the red strip into the safety column because the color looked official. The supervisor crossed out the mistaken code and retained the owner identifier separately. Yue watched him preserve the error as an audit mark instead of making the page appear always correct.

shoal_e02_rejoin_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_08.text: The correction mattered to Rong because a rejected safety label could keep a sound part from reaching a paying customer. It mattered to the owner because a personal repair mark could vanish in a public inventory. Neither needed to lose for the other to be heard. The actual part still required a qualified test. Removing a mistaken label did not certify it as safe. Yue found the distinction harder to maintain aloud than on paper, where separate columns did some of the thinking.

shoal_e02_rejoin_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_09.text: After the visit, the supervisor named a condition for Yue's acceptance. She would not conduct powered work alone, and any fatigue or altered grip ended that day's technical assignment even if fewer than thirty shifts had been completed. Paid permitted restricted tasks could replace some hours only if defined before the shift. The port account did not purchase a body that had to produce the same result every day. Yue asked him to add who authorized the replacement task.

shoal_e02_rejoin_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_10.text: Han's draft gave that authority jointly to the qualified supervisor and the restoration wage receiver, with a recorded worker agreement. A rejected powered shift could become ordinary labeling, sorting, or return preparation within the same bounded batch. It could not become roof work because a merchant was in a hurry. The change protected the budget as well as Yue. Nobody could disguise a hazardous new task under an old day's signature and claim it had already been priced.

shoal_e02_rejoin_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_11.text: Outside the store, Yan directed a team hauling a warped spar from a cradle. The team used two ordinary purchase lines and an inspected ground anchor. Yue stood behind the marked observer rope. A crew member joked that six primary pairs should make the spar feel embarrassed. Yan told him the spar had no opinion and the anchor did. The joke ended without requiring Yue to display modesty or prowess. The line remained the line.

shoal_e02_rejoin_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_12.text: The spar shifted unexpectedly when a hidden knot released from the support. The crew stopped on Yan's shouted instruction and settled its weight into the prepared crib. A man lost his cap into a puddle; no one leaped after the spar. Afterward, they inspected the anchor and changed the support spacing before resuming. Yue could see why the observer rope was farther back than a casual visitor would have placed it. The safe exit needed room for an unplanned movement.

shoal_e02_rejoin_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_13.text: Yan asked Yue what she had observed, not what she thought the crew should have done. She described the knot release, the first shouted stop, and the crib contact. She had not seen the far-side support before the movement, so she could not compare its earlier position. He wrote her limits beside her account. A truthful narrow witness might be more useful than a confident visitor who filled the missing angle from a later view.

shoal_e02_rejoin_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_14.text: The cap's owner wrung it out and asked whether the shifted spar would delay his afternoon wage. Yan said the crew's separately funded inspection pause remained paid under their current terms. He could not promise the merchant would keep every later commission. Yue noticed how quickly safe work turned into an economic question. A prepared stop was easier to use when people knew stopping would not immediately cost dinner. Her own proposal needed that clarity too.

shoal_e02_rejoin_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_15.text: Song Mei passed the yard with two other performers carrying wrapped instruments. She greeted Yue but did not stop in the hauling lane. Her provisional public slot remained subject to the venue's inspection and her own terms with its keeper. She was not available as an impromptu witness to the spar movement, which she had not seen. Yue asked whether the public notice was still current. Song Mei said it was current enough to read, and that was all she could promise today.

shoal_e02_rejoin_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_16.text: They shared a short walk to the lane junction. Song Mei described a borrowed room whose acoustics were poor and whose keeper nevertheless wanted a share of every sale of a performance sheet. She had declined that clause. No one had withdrawn a cultivation benefit from Yue because a performer refused a contract. Song Mei might find another room or postpone the piece. Her art had costs and owners that did not dissolve merely because their roads had met again.

shoal_e02_rejoin_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_17.text: At the junction, Song Mei turned toward her own appointment. Yue wanted to ask about the coming story and realized the question would make the performer late. She let the invitation remain public. It felt like a small loss because she had hoped for a friend amid official introductions. Friendship could survive an hour that was not offered. Yue returned to the partnership room carrying the supervisor's amended draft rather than a conversation she had extracted through affection.

shoal_e02_rejoin_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_18.text: On Day Two Hundred Twenty-Five, the public wage receiver reviewed the arrival allocation's final eight copper. Each named receiving duty had been performed and signed at its actual time. No money remained in that grant for a traveler who stayed longer. The sixteen-copper eight-night housing payment was already settled. Yue's own subsequent six-copper extension remained separate. Han placed the closed arrival account below the still unsigned restoration proposal so that the page order would not imply a financial bridge.

shoal_e02_rejoin_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_19.text: The license keeper asked for Yue's next housing answer before evening. She could extend the same lodging at the posted rate from her own money while deciding about work, or take a paid bed elsewhere. Her earlier social choice did not compel indefinite residence. Yue reserved three more nights, Days Two Hundred Twenty-Six through Twenty-Eight, and paid six copper herself. The room would remain available while she made a real employment decision, with no debt hidden behind a welcoming phrase.

shoal_e02_rejoin_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_20.text: A boy at the public board had erased a lane closure while copying the map for a school lesson. He thought the cross mark meant a drawing mistake. The teacher corrected the copy and apologized to the gate attendant whose sign had been rubbed away. The original temporary notice was restored. Yue helped hold the paper flat while the teacher wrote the review time. The children were learning a city that changed under their pencils, not a permanent diagram every adult already knew.

shoal_e02_rejoin_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_21.text: One child asked why a closed lane was still shown on the map. The teacher said people needed to know where they could not go as well as where they could. Another asked why the alternate route was longer for wheelbarrows. A dock worker drew the curb where a loaded cart could not turn. Yue listened. Her new port access had made ordinary public teaching available, but she had not become its instructor by standing close enough to answer a question.

shoal_e02_rejoin_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_22.text: Later, a supplier sent a request to start an unloaded comparison before the accepted work term. The supervisor rejected it because Yue had not signed employment, the borrowed or public source permissions differed by her incoming terms, and the shift lacked its funded setup. The request was preserved as declined rather than moved into next week's completed column. A useful outcome could not travel backward to create the agreement that would have made its first step proper.

shoal_e02_rejoin_23.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_23.text: Yue spent the remaining days before the acceptance meeting checking the lane closures and the published clinical hours. She did not discover a grand secret in the harbor's gaps. She found an unreadable time, an outdated keeper's name, and a desk that closed half an hour before a worker's shift ended. Each needed a different person to change it. She sent the public corrections to their owners and left the unpaid private investigation she had imagined unstarted.

shoal_e02_rejoin_24.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_24.text: At the partnership room, the forty housings had acquired the three proposed containers and a night guard schedule funded from the named materials and supervisor scope. Owner return decisions remained separate. The anonymous guarding question had been added to the public draft with its permission mark; the asker was not identified. Public definitions of canceled requests were also available through the clerk. Different paths of access had brought partial facts to the same bounded problem without making those paths equivalent.

shoal_e02_rejoin_25.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_25.text: The coughing dock hand attended his dated follow-up and chose not to share its result with the public room. His employer continued the work arrangement it actually accepted. Yue did not narrate a recovery she could not verify. Sui needed only the applicable work clearance, conveyed privately through the correct desk. A story about harbor safety could leave one person's medical ending unspoken and still explain why access rules, wages, and clinical authority must not be merged.

shoal_e02_rejoin_26.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_26.text: On Day Two Hundred Thirty-One, the supervisor laid an acceptance copy beside the amended draft. The scope still covered thirty shifts across six weeks and forty unloaded housings. Funded ordinary care did not guarantee bodily repair. Qualified tests could reject everything in a row. If Yue took the post, her first paid shift would begin tomorrow. She could still refuse tonight and pay for her next room from her own savings. The proposal finally stood far enough apart from arrival hospitality to be a choice.

shoal_e02_rejoin_27.speaker: narrator
shoal_e02_rejoin_27.text: She read the page outside, where the tide could be heard beyond the store walls. It was not the kind of work that would make a harbor cheer. Results would be marks on parts, and some would cost their owners a replacement. Yet the boundaries made it possible to tell whether Yue had helped. She folded the copy without signing it in the lane. Tomorrow she would answer beside the people responsible for the work, with its refusals written where everyone saw them.
